rationale: bugs_open/154: tool-auditor-raised improve_tool items die at tool-improver's first step with 'query param path input_data.component_id resolved to nil', while items from three other creators run clean. The bug file recorded the tell — the failures are the rows whose component_id IS set — and marked its explanation [INFERRED], instructing the fixing thread to read the dispatch mapping and the load_tool step first. I did. The cause is not in either agent: site_work_items carries component_id, entity_id and affected_url as first-class columns, but LoadWorkItemsAction builds current_item from a SELECT that lists only page_id among them. So the only path a dispatcher can reference is current_item.spec.<key> — a copy the creating agent must remember to duplicate into the spec JSONB. build-dispatch-loop maps 'component_id?': 'current_item.spec.component_id'; ResolveInputMapping treats the ? suffix as optional and silently skips an unresolved path; tool-improver's load_tool then hard-errors on the nil param. The creator that used the schema properly is precisely the one whose items cannot be dispatched. This change makes the item map expose those three columns top-level, resolved column-first with a spec.<key> fallback, so ONE dispatcher path is correct for both populations — input_mapping resolves exactly one source path per destination and has no coalesce syntax, which is why the coalesce must live in Go. Intent is to close the door on the class, not to patch one agent: any future creator that populates a first-class routing column now produces a dispatchable item by construction. NOTE, round 2: round 1 was rejected at persist_submission — 'edit 4: file path must be repo-relative with no traversal or whitespace'. That was correct and entirely my fault: I had put a prose description in the file field to mark the config change as living in the DB rather than the repo. It is now a real migration file, which is what it should have been anyway — a config change nobody can read or roll back is not reviewable. No reviewer time was spent on round 1; the plan is otherwise unchanged.

plan.summary: site_work_items.component_id/entity_id/affected_url are real columns that no handler can see, because LoadWorkItemsAction never selects them into the current_item map. Work items carrying the column and not the spec copy are structurally undispatchable — the optional dispatch mapping skips silently and the handler's first query_database dies on a nil param. This exposes the three columns top-level on the item map, column-first with a spec fallback, plus a regression test. page_id is deliberately left column-only and spec is deliberately never mutated; both non-changes are argued from measurements below.

edits.rationale: The coalesce has to live in Go because input_mapping resolves exactly one source path per destination and has no coalesce syntax — without it the config must choose which half of the fleet's work items it can route. Column-first because the column is the typed, indexed source and spec is a hand-maintained copy that can go stale. The key is left ABSENT rather than set to "" when neither source has a value: the dispatch mapping marks these optional ("component_id?"), and ResolveInputMapping forwards a path that RESOLVES while skipping one that is MISSING — so materialising "" would turn 'not supplied' into 'supplied as empty' for handlers that gate on presence, e.g. create_rerender_items' `componentIDStr != ""`. A non-string under the same spec key is refused rather than forwarded to a uuid parse.

Select and scan the three first-class routing columns, then expose them via setRoutingField. Appended at the end of both the SELECT list and the Scan target list so the existing column/scan alignment is untouched — a misalignment here is not a loud failure: the scan error path drops the row through a `continue` while find_dispatchable_site still counts it, which is the bugs_closed/078 livelock. That is exactly what the end-to-end test pins.
edits.sketch:
@@ SELECT list @@
 			wi.batch_id, wi.attempt_count,
 			COALESCE(wi.approval_mode, 'auto') as approval_mode,
+			wi.component_id, wi.entity_id, wi.affected_url
@@ scan vars @@
 			approvalMode               string
+			// First-class routing columns — all nullable, hence pointers.
+			componentID, entityID *uuid.UUID
+			affectedURL           sql.NullString
@@ rows.Scan @@
 			&batchID, &attemptCount, &approvalMode,
+			&componentID, &entityID, &affectedURL,
@@ item map build @@
+		setRoutingField(item, "component_id", uuidPtrString(componentID), logger)
+		setRoutingField(item, "entity_id", uuidPtrString(entityID), logger)
+		setRoutingField(item, "affected_url", affectedURL.String, logger)
 		if pageID != nil {
 			item["page_id"] = pageID.String()
 		}

edits.rationale: Pins the resolution order, the absent-not-empty property, the no-spec-mutation property (which is the guard on the rejected design — a later 'tidy-up' that backfills spec would reintroduce the rerender-scoping hazard), and an end-to-end sqlmock case over the real SELECT and real Scan so the two cannot drift apart. Proven non-vacuous by induced fault: deleting the component_id exposure line makes TestLoadWorkItems_ExposesRoutingColumns fail on BOTH the column-only row and the spec-only row.
edits.sketch: New file. Table-driven cases: column-set/spec-missing -> column value (the 154 case); column-empty/spec-set -> spec value (the 235-row majority); both set -> column wins; neither -> key ABSENT not ""; spec holds non-string or "" -> absent. Plus TestSetRoutingField_NeverMutatesSpec asserting spec is unchanged, TestSetRoutingField_ToleratesAbsentSpec for nil/scalar spec, and TestLoadWorkItems_ExposesRoutingColumns driving the action through sqlmock with all 19 columns and asserting page_id stays absent on a row whose column is NULL.

edits.rationale: The config half of the fix, written as a reviewable migration rather than a hand-run UPDATE. Applied to the live agent_definitions row AFTER the image ships, never before: the coalesce lives in the binary, so flipping this first would strand the 235 spec-only rows on a chassis that cannot resolve current_item.component_id — strictly worse than the bug. Guarded three ways: jsonb_set with create_missing=false so a drifted mapping fails loud instead of growing a second key, a WHERE clause matching the exact prior value so it is idempotent and refuses a row that is not the shape this was written against, and a documented pod-grep with a positive control as the gate on applying it at all. Declared to the council so the review covers the whole change, not just the half that happens to be Go.

plan.risks: 1) The change newly DELIVERS component_id to handlers for the 16 column-set items, which is the point but is still a widening. I checked the two other affected handlers rather than asserting safety: section-editor reads page_component_id and never input_data.component_id (inert); rerender-pages reads input_data.spec.component_id, which this change does not touch at all, precisely because create_rerender_items gates its scoping on it. 2) page_id is deliberately NOT given the spec fallback — 218 rows would newly gain current_item.page_id. A reviewer may reasonably argue the asymmetry is a wart; my position is that symmetry is not a reason to widen 218 items' handler inputs, and the comment records the measurement so a future thread can revisit it with evidence. 3) Column/scan alignment is the one silent failure mode (a mis-scan drops the row via `continue` and re-selects the site forever — bugs_closed/078); the end-to-end sqlmock test exists to catch exactly that and was induced-fault proven. 4) The config half is ordered after the image; if a thread applies it early the 235 spec-only rows lose their component_id until the roll. 5) NOT fixed here and recorded in the bug file: tool-auditor's item_key is site-scoped ('audit_fix_<domain>'), so it cannot express which tool it is fixing and rows accumulate once one goes terminal. That is a separate defect in item creation with fleet-wide dedup consequences; it wants its own measurement and review rather than riding along.
